title: Free-vertex derived internal Hom and its telescope endomorphism
statement: Let J be a small site with commutative coefficient ring sheaf R, U an object, f a section on U, and K a derived module complex. Assume derived categories on the base and slice and a product of the copies of L=K restricted to U. For P and d from [lem-weil-pbc-local-coefficient-telescope], there exists an isomorphism from derived internal Hom of P[0] into L [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] to the product of the copies of L indexed by natural numbers. It intertwines precomposition by d with the endomorphism 1-shift of the tower with transition multiplication by f [def-weil-derived-limit, def-weil-pbc-local-coefficient-localization]. Module sheaves are understood as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Derived categories are as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: Choose a representative of L on the slice and a K-injective resolution there. The natural representative comparison for derived internal Hom reduces the claim to the Hom-complex from P[0] into this resolution I. No preservation of injectivity under slice restriction is required.

proof.text: Projecting to the sole nonzero source degree of P[0] identifies the Hom-complex with degreewise internal Hom from P, using homComplex_projections_exists. Apply the already proved ordinary product property [lem-weil-pbc-countable-free-internal-hom-product] in each degree. The Hom-complex differential is coordinatewise because the single source has zero differential. The projections are precomposition with basis inclusions followed by evaluation at 1.

proof.text: The termwise product of K-injective complexes, with its coordinate projections, represents the product in the derived category. Transport this product cone along QI≅L and compare it with the specified product by its universal property.

source.place: Tag 0997, proof of lemma-hom-from-Af, equivalence (1) and (3).

proof.text: Precomposing a family with d(e_n)=e_n-f e_(n+1) gives its n-th coordinate pr_n-f pr_(n+1). The representative comparison is natural in the source. Naturality of scalar multiplication, first along the resolution map and then along the derived restriction comparison, identifies the scalar chain endomorphism with the given localSectionDerivedMultiplication component. Product extensionality gives the asserted intertwining equation. This uses no exactness of infinite products and remains valid for f=0, a unit f, and the zero ring.

mathlib_searches.query: In a category of sheaves of modules, the localization at a section is the cokernel of the telescope on a countable free module; derived internal Hom from that free module is the product of the target complexes.
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: SheafOfModules.free, iFree, hasLimit, free presentations and HasDerivedCategory.standard. These supply the elementary constructions, but none is the telescope exact sequence or the derived-Hom product comparison.

theorem localCoefficientFreeDerivedHom_product
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (U : C) (f : R.obj.obj (op U))
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u} (localCoefficientRings R))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wSlice} (ringedSiteModules.{u} ((localCoefficientRings R).over U))]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ringedSiteModules.{u} (localCoefficientRings R)))
    [HasProduct (fun _ : ℕ ↦ (localCoefficientDerivedRestriction R U).obj K)] :
    let L := (localCoefficientDerivedRestriction R U).obj K
    let H := (Functor.curry.obj (derivedInternalHom (J.over U) (R.over U))).flip.obj L
    ∃ e : H.obj (op ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
        (localCoefficientFreeSum R U))) ≅ ∏ᶜ (fun _ : ℕ ↦ L),
      H.map ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).map
        (localCoefficientTelescopeMap R U f)).op ≫ e.hom =
      e.hom ≫ towerTransitionEndomorphism
        (fun _ ↦ (localSectionDerivedMultiplication R U f).app K)
